articles.title: Agnes Callamard: US sanctions vs ICC could jeopardize Rodrigo Duterte case
articles.summary: 'There is only one response to the USA threats and sanctions: it must be protecting the ICC. Not appeasing the predator,' Callamard says

blocks.text: LAUNCH. Amnesty International Secretary General Agnès Callamard calls for justice for drug war victims during the November 20 launch of 'Walang Pahimakas' in Quezon City, on November 20, 2026.
Mia Magdalena-Fokno
'There is only one response to the USA threats and sanctions: it must be protecting the ICC. Not appeasing the predator,' Callamard says

items: Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International's secretary general, warned that US sanctions against the ICC could put at risk its operations and the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte.
Callamard emphasized that if the ICC cannot function due to these sanctions, it risks losing its credibility and independence.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Amnesty International secretary general and human rights activist Agnes Callamard warned that the United States’ sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) could imperil the court’s operations, including the case of former president Rodrigo Duterte.

At the sidelines of the event, the Amnesty secretary general told Palawan News that these sanctions could cause the collapse of the court. “If the ICC is unable to function, the ICC will collapse. Or the trial will deliver the verdict that will have lost its credibility. At all levels, whether it’s operational or political, it’s bad news.”

Callamard was in the Philippines for Rappler’s Social Good Summit on Saturday, November 20, where she and other advocates talked about the need to build a community amid threats of Artificial Intelligence. As United Nations Special Rapporteur on Extrajudicial Killings, she was barred by the Duterte administration from entering the country. The Marcos government lifted this ban only last September.

Callamard told Rappler, “The trial of ex-president Duterte is due to start on 30 November. It could take one year or probably more until judgment. If no action is taken to protect the ICC against the US sanctions, the trial may never proceed.”

In an interview with Rappler, Callamard said: “I was told that just this week, in a meeting of the state parties to the ICC, the diplomats of the most powerful countries, including Canada and the UK, and other G7 states, have insisted the only way forward is to negotiate with the US and agree to their demands. They continue to refuse to protect the ICC.”
According to Callamard, the US is giving the ICC until April to comply with the following:

items: No ICC jurisdiction over non-state parties or “an impunity carve-out for the USA”
Dropping of ICC investigations and arrest warrants in the Palestine situation
Immunities for heads of state

blocks.text: The Amnesty secretary general said that if the powerful countries that are part of the ICC “are prepared to negotiate with the US, the ICC will lose its independence and credibility.”

“The failure to protect the ICC is a betrayal of the mothers and fathers, sons and daughters of the Philippines that have spoken up against Duterte’s senseless war, against threats and intimidation,” she added.

Duterte has been detained in The Hague, Netherlands since March 2025 after he was arrested due to three counts of crimes against humanity case. His case stemmed from the alleged killings of the Davao Death Squad and his bloody war on drugs that killed nearly 30,000 people, according to several human rights organizations.
In April, the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I confirmed all three charges against the former president. His trial will start on November 30 at the ICC Trial Chamber III.

blocks.caption: ICC wraps up pre-trial hearings as Duterte’s November 30 case nears

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump, in the last years, has been pushing to sanction the ICC which has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and crimes of aggression.

In February 2025, Trump authorized economic and travel sanctions against those involved in the ICC probe into US citizens or allies like Israel. He imposed sanctions, in the same year, against four ICC judges over the issuance of an arrest warrant for Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu and a past decision to open a case into alleged war crimes by US troops in Afghanistan.

Just last August, the US government imposed sanctions against ICC President Tomoko Akane and Abdoulaye Seye, a senior ICC trial lawyer. But the most concerning development is the ICC-wide sanctions that the Trump administration is planning to announce soon.

Entity-wide sanctions would bar US citizens and companies from giving the ICC funds, goods, or services without permission from the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control. This would be tricky because banks often comply with these sanctions since they are dependent on access to the American financial system, according to Reuters.
Apart from this, ICC-wide sanctions could affect the court’s IT services and insurance, investigations, and payments to employees.

blocks.caption: Trump administration prepares sanctions vs ICC, sources say

blocks.text: Callamard urged European governments to “use their ‘blocking’ law, which bars European companies from complying with foreign sanctions. She also called on central banks in Europe to give the court bank accounts,” Palawan News reported.

She told Rappler: “There is only one response to the USA threats and sanctions: it must be protecting the ICC. Not appeasing the predator. They continue to refuse to protect the ICC. They are betraying decades of efforts forged in blood and tears to ensure that no one, absolutely no one should be above the law.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct
articles.summary: The Philippines wanted a South China Sea code of conduct in place by 2026. But persistent disagreements between China and ASEAN countries are slowing progress toward a deal.

image.caption: Chinese missile frigate Yuncheng launches an anti-ship missile during a military exercise in the waters near south China's Hainan Island and Paracel IslandsImage: Zha Chunming/Xinhua/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: It was supposed to be a breakthrough year. The Philippines had intended to set up a code of conduct with China for the South China Sea during its 2026 ASEAN presidency. However, at the summit in Manila in mid-November they had to abandon their goal. Some 80% of the text had been negotiated, declared Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, but the key areas of dispute had remained unsolved.

Much more than diplomatic wording is at stake. The South China Sea is one of the world's most important shipping routes, it is rich in fishing grounds and may harbor significant oil and gas reserves. Primarily, however, it's a region of strategic competition: With its so-called Nine-Dash Line (often drawn in red), China claims a large portion of the sea. Its claims overlap with those of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.

A code of conduct is to set up rules for parties dealing with one another and prevent incidents at sea from escalating. However, opinions differ, particularly with regard to its binding nature and its geographic scope.

"The basic problem with establishing such a code of conduct is that China is supremely powerful and has no real interest in a legally binding agreement," said political scientist Andreas Ufen, Southeast Asia expert at the German Institute of Global and Area Studies (GIGA). Beijing had little incentive to impose restrictions on itself as long as it was able to pursue its interests in the region even without such an agreement, Ufen told DW.

blocks.caption: The 2026 ASEAN summit in Manila Image: Reuters

blocks.text: Mere recommendations or legally binding set of rules?

The Paracel Islands serve as an example of just how difficult the unresolved issues are. In China, the group of islands is known as Xisha, in Vietnam as Hoang-Sa. Hanoi apparently wants to include them in the code's geographic scope, but China rejects this. An agreement within the ASEAN framework could indirectly affect the territorial claims of the parties involved.

"A fundamental problem is that so far there's no consensus on whether the code of conduct should be legally binding," said Felix Heiduk, head of research division Asia at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP). China and the ASEAN nations have been negotiating an agreement for 12 years without major progress so far.

There were reservations about such a treaty not only in China but also in other ASEAN countries. They would subsequently have to ratify a legally binding agreement under international law in their own countries. A non-binding code of conduct, by contrast, would be little more than a voluntary declaration of intent, Ufen told DW.

The definition of an "incident" is controversial as well. Are coast guard missions with use of water cannons included? Or blockades of supply vessels? Or is the code only applicable when military force is involved? This will determine which actions will be covered by the regulations in the future.

"These are by no means just technical details. Their clarification determines to a great extent whether the code of conduct will in fact be effective or will ultimately remain only a non-binding declaration of intent," Heiduk said. An agreement without valid commitments would bring about little change.
How a small, disputed island wards off China's power claims
Diverging interests

Ufen views China's attitude as a strategic calculation. "I believe that China is interested in keeping the conflict simmering, so to speak, without having to commit itself to a truly binding legal regulation," he said. In this way, Beijing could strengthen its position in the South China Sea without limiting its room for maneuver.

At the same time there are also diverging interests within the ASEAN group. The 11 member states are by no means united. The Philippines and Vietnam are particularly vocal in their opposition to China. Malaysia and Indonesia pursue a more restrained approach. Cambodia and Laos have close economic ties with Beijing and don't have any territorial claims in the South China Sea.

"From the start of the negotiations, the lack of unity within ASEAN has been a problem. In a way, it's a permanent obstacle," Heiduk said. The group makes decisions based on the consensus principle, which basically means that every member state can block a unified position. Recurring confrontations between China and the Philippines exacerbated the problem by undermining trust and making it more difficult to reach compromises.

Ufen also believes that diverging interests are a key impediment. "Reconciling them is extremely difficult," he said. China could take advantage of the discord. Beijing preferred bilateral negotiations with individual countries rather than dealing with an entire, united group of nations.
Fundamental conflicts unresolved

A study published by the Singapore-based Yusof Ishak Institute (ISEAS)reaches similar conclusions. Not only China but internal divisions within ASEAN stalled negotiations. The authors warn against exclusively relying on a comprehensive, legally binding treaty. Initially, partial agreements — for example, on crisis communication, rescue operations at sea or maritime environment protection — could be a first step. Developing the 2002 agreement on a non-binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea could also be an intermediate step.

blocks.caption: A Chinese Coast Guard and a Philippine Navy vessel during an encounter in the South China Sea on July 20, 2026Image: Jay Tarriela via X/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Ufen doubts whether Beijing is interested in a binding result. "For this reason, I can't really imagine that China has a real interest in a code of conduct that includes legally binding regulations," he said.

Heiduk warns against overestimating the significance of a potential agreement. "Even if the code of conduct was signed at some point, in whichever shape, that would in no way solve the conflict in the South China Sea," he said. The code could regulate how to handle incidents, but it could not eliminate territorial disputes and competing claims to maritime areas.
Can ASEAN do more to stop the violence in Myanmar?
Hopes for future negotiations

This constitutes the dilemma for ASEAN nations as well, whose foreign policy oscillates between China and US ties: An agreement that's as binding as possible could fail because China and individual member states have reservations. A weak, non-binding code, however, could give the impression everyone agreed but would hardly change conduct at sea.

The American Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) summed up the situationafter the summit in Manila: "Whatever progress was made this year, it is almost certain that the hardest sticking points remain unresolved."

Negotiations will be continued in 2027 under Singapore's chairmanship. Whether this will turn into more than just another diplomatic effort will depend on whether China is prepared to submit itself to regulations which limit its scope of action and whether ASEAN will be able to reach a consensus.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Prosecution ready should VP Sara, Mans Carpio testify in impeachment court - Joel Chua
articles.summary: The prosecution is ready should Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, testify before the impeachment court, House lead prosecutor and Manila 3rd District Representative Joel…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 4:44pm

The prosecution is ready should Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, testify before the impeachment court, House lead prosecutor and Manila 3rd District Representative Joel Chua said, as senator-judges aim to secure a verdict before the year ends.

“While we are anticipating that [na haharap si VP Duterte/Atty. Mans Carpio] na possible, dahil kagaya ng sinasabi namin from the very beginning, sila lang ang makakasagot nang lahat ng isyung 'to. Kung sila man ang ipepresenta, naka-ready naman kami,” Chua told Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday.

(While we are anticipating that VP Duterte and Atty. Mans Carpio may appear, as we have been saying from the very beginning, they are the only ones who can answer all these issues. If they are presented as witnesses, we are ready.)

On the 45th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial, defense witness and Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., a listed business interest of Carpio, is a registered micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) despite millions in money flows.
The Senate impeachment court has moved the trial dates from November 26 and 27 to December 1, 2, 3, and 4 due to the unavailability of defense witnesses.
Chua expressed satisfaction with the witnesses presented by the defense, saying that their testimonoes and actions are helping the prosecution in winning the case.
“Masaya kami sa mga testigo na ipiniprisinta nila dahil sa tingin namin ay maganda naman ang nagiging performance sa pagtulong sa amin,” Chua said.
(We are pleased with the witnesses the defense has presented because we believe they have been performing well in helping our case.)
“So far, nakakailang testigo na sila, so far wala pa silang naiprepresentang substantial,” he added.
(So far, they have presented several witnesses, but they have yet to offer anything substantial.)

He explained that the prosecution's case focuses on the P817 million in allegedly undeclared wealth in Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), not the issue of whether Cale88 is a registered business or not.
“Hindi namin kinukuwestiyon ang pagiging rehistrado ng Cale88. Ang isyu rito ay yung hindi idineklarang income,” Chua said.
(We are not questioning whether Cale88 is registered. The issue here is the income that was not declared.)
“Dahil ang Article 2 ay about unexplained wealth. Walang kaugnayan kung rehistrado 'yan o hindi. Ang pinag-uusapan dito, ito bang kinita sa Cale 88 ay isinama sa SALN,” he added.
(Article 2 is about unexplained wealth. Whether it is registered or not is irrelevant. The question is whether the income earned from Cale88 was included in the SALN.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
articles.summary: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the…

image.caption: The Goodforces provides digital space for progressive political campaigns on social mediaImage: Neunund20/the Goodforces

blocks.text: Red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

blocks.caption: Patrick Haermeyer got his inspiration from working with the campaign of US Senator Bernie SandersImage: Karol Roller

blocks.text: Content creation, sharing, networking, campaigning

Neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" issues.

Users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer says physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

The Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.
Germany's public broadcasters under fire from far-right AfD
Super PAC-style campaigning is new in Germany

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting new type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.
What's behind the rising polarization in German politics?

Haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.
That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

"We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles."
Stemming the rise of far-right AfD with digital know-how

The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

The social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's new military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.
Agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.
Why Germany's political center is losing ground
Big-tent parties in Germany in decline for decades
Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

"It is an omission of the parties," he said. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open."

The center-left and center-right big-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

Party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) showed that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

In the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

The political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures."

articles.title: Highly lucrative: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
articles.summary:
New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people

•

blocks.text: British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.
In the 1840s, Cuba was the most important foreign source of copper ore for the UK. Copper was critical to Manchester’s cotton industry, railways and telegraphy.
Previous research has revealed that dozens of financiers involved in the founding in 1694 of the Bank of England invested in enslavement.
Now, Evans’s research reveals that ties between key figures in the UK’s financial system and enslavement of African peoples continued even after the government outlawed it.
Britain abolished its trade in enslaved people in 1807 and passed legislation abolishing slavery in most of its empire in 1833.

However, as Britain’s Slavery Abolition Act was coming into force, “City of London figures” were developing mining of El Cobre’s copper ore deposits, an operation which depended on enslavement in Spanish-controlled Cuba.
Key players in the highly lucrative operation included the Bank of England directors Charles Pascoe Grenfell (1790-1867) and William Thompson (1792-1854), acting in a private capacity.

Enslaved copper miners at El Cobre were likely to have been trafficked to Cuba by illegal voyages from the Bight of Biafra, in modern-day Nigeria, as Evans details in his book, Slavery’s Long Goodbye – Capitalism, Nationalism and Christianity in the Age of British Emancipation.

The death rate at El Cobre means it is likely that thousands of Africans were exploited there. Their life stories remain largely undocumented. At the time, slavery was legal in Cuba but the importation of enslaved people was not.
As a partner in the Cobre mining and export company, Grenfell was a driving force in enslaved miners’ exploitation.

Cobre was “likely to be the largest slave enterprise in the western hemisphere” by the 1840s, Evans said. Investors who held Cobre shares from the outset received £102 in dividends for every £40 share between 1836 and 1865.

blocks.caption: Enslavement at El Cobre ended after Cuban revolutionaries captured the town from Spanish forces in November 1868. Illustration: Amgueddfa Cymru/National Museum of Wales

blocks.text: Grenfell was also a partner in a Swansea-based smelter Pascoe, Grenfell & Sons, which bought imports from the mine, in an era when the Welsh port was the centre of the global copper trade.
Meanwhile, Thompson, a former lord mayor of London, exploited enslaved miners through the ore export firm he directed, the Royal Santiago Company.

The UK is facing increased pressure to make a formal apology to Caribbean and African nations for Britain’s centuries-long perpetuation of transatlantic chattel slavery. Commonwealth leaders say “structured dialogue” with the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, will begin in the next year.

While the Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has claimed Britain has nothing to apologise for, scholarship – dating back to the Trinidadian statesman Eric Williams’s 1944 book, Capitalism and Slavery – reveals the global impact of the colonialism and chattel enslavement that was integral to British capitalism’s success.

Evans, a former professor at the University of South Wales, said: “As Britain ostentatiously winds down its own slave system in the 1830s, British capital is boosting slavery elsewhere in the western hemisphere.

“The illegal trade, involving French and Spanish merchants, was flourishing and substantial. There were British (anti-slavery) patrols off the coast of Cuba, but they’re relatively few in number and intercept only a very small proportion of slave ships.”
Conditions at El Cobre were “extremely brutal”, with daily violence and torture. “Slave catchers” were employed to snatch miners who tried to escape to the mountains.
after newsletter promotion

In 1817, under British pressure, Spanish authorities signed a treaty that banned trafficking enslaved Africans to Cuba. But as Cuba’s sugar and coffee plantations relied on enslaved African workers, local colonial authorities ignored it, with 25,000 captives arriving in 1859 alone.

blocks.caption: Charles Grenfell was a partner in a Swansea-based smelter Pascoe, Grenfell & Sons, which bought imports from Cuba. Illustration: Digitised by Bethan Jones/Amgueddfa Cymru/National Museum of Wales

blocks.text: In 1843, pressure from the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society prompted legislation intended to prohibit British subjects from owning enslaved people in other jurisdictions, after undercover investigations exposed British mining companies’ activities in Brazil and Cuba, including at El Cobre.

But after lobbying by mining interests, parliament diluted the legislation, allowing companies to retain enslaved workers as their “property” and hire others. The concessions prompted abolitionists to withdraw their support for the law, which failed to end the exploitation.

Neither Grenfell nor Thompson appears to have faced legal penalties for their involvement. Grenfell became the Liberal MP for Preston in the late 1840s, later boasting that his father had been an abolitionist. Grenfell remained a B of E director until 1864.

Enslavement at El Cobre finally ended after Cuban revolutionaries captured the town from Spanish forces in November 1868. The rebel commander proclaimed the miners’ emancipation on New Year’s Eve, and formerly enslaved workers later joined Cuba’s liberation army.
Evans’s book explores Britain’s overlapping histories of slavery, capitalism and missionary Christianity through the lives of Grenfell and two of his cousins.
Evans added: “The British in the early 19th century had started to understand slavery as a national sin.
“In the classical age of abolition, you could do things like abstain from eating sugar from the West Indies.

“But with copper, you can’t do that because it’s embodied in the industrial world, and, in the age of joint-stock capitalism, you have many British people who invest in mining companies who genuinely didn’t know these companies were using enslaved workers.

“Slavery was rendered invisible by the complexity of industrial society. But British engagement with slavery continued long after Emancipation. It involved the mercantile-financial elite of London as well as hundreds, possibly thousands, of rank-and-file investors from the Victorian middle class.”
A Bank of England spokesperson said: “We have previously acknowledged the role of former governors and directors in the slave trade.”

articles.summary: Executive Secretary Ralph Recto on Sunday commended the Philippines" “successful hosting” of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, stressing the need to follow through on agreements reached…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 3:52pm

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto on Sunday commended the Philippines’ “successful hosting” of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, stressing the need to follow through on agreements reached during the meetings.
In a statement, Recto, who chairs the ASEAN National Organizing Council, thanked government agencies and other partners that helped organize the summit.

“Led and guided by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., the Philippines successfully hosted the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, which were international in productive participation and global in positive impact,” Recto said.

“As Chair of the ASEAN National Organizing Council, I salute the hard work and long hours put in by government agencies and partners to carry out the President’s directive of a summit and meetings that showcase our country’s best and the ASEAN spirit of solidarity,” he added.
The Philippines, which holds the rotating chairmanship of ASEAN this year, hosted the 48th and 49th ASEAN Summits in May and November, respectively.
Recto said the summit's success should also be measured by how the agreements reached would benefit the country and its people.
He cited the Philippines' hosting of two new ASEAN centers for creative industries and maritime cooperation as among the key outcomes of the meetings.
“The one for creative industries will incubate great startups. The maritime cooperation center, on the other hand, will help advance negotiations on the South China Sea Code of Conduct,” Recto said.
He noted that despite the hundreds of meetings held during the summit, several key agreements still needed to be finalized and implemented.
“The summit may be over, and the fanfare may have died down. But the work that follows is no less important than the work that brought us here—and deserves no less dedication,” Recto said.
“Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat. Karangalan ng Pilipinas ang tagumpay na ito. At dapat bawat Pilipino ang makinabang sa bunga ng ating pagsisikap,” he added.
(Thank you very much to all of you. This success is an honor for the Philippines. And every Filipino should benefit from the fruits of our hard work.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: US: ICE arrests 2 at Seattle airport in 'chilling' scenes — governor
articles.summary: Washington's governor has denounced the arrests made by ICE officers at Seattle's airport, calling the incident "horrific."

image.caption: ANti-ICE protesters confronted police at the airport after the arrestsImage: David Ryder/REUTERS

blocks.text: Masked US immigration officers have detained two people on an airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles, prompting criticism from Washington state Governor Bob Ferguson and concerns from Alaska Airlines.

The arrests took place at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport around 8 a.m. local time (1600 UTC) on Saturday. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said the operation targeted Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who had overstayed his visa.

Agents also arrested Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who they alleged threw hot coffee at the ICE officers during the confrontation. ICE said she had also overstayed her visa and would face a charge of assaulting a federal officer.
When ICE comes knocking: the fight against Trump's deportations

Videos of the incident circulated on social media, showing officers struggling with a person on the ground as passengers look on. One woman could be heard shouting that her daughter was being taken away and that she had a work permit.
Washington governor slams 'out of control' ICE
Governor Ferguson, a Democrat, described the footage as "horrific" and "chilling", accusing ICE of being "completely and totally out of control."
He urged Alaska Airlines to ask federal immigration authorities to leave the state's airports and said he would make the same appeal to other airlines operating at Seattle-Tacoma.
Alaska Airlines said it had received no advance notice of the enforcement operation and was working to understand the circumstances.
The airline also expressed concern over the incident, which it said had been distressing for passengers and employees.

The operation drew criticism from April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, who said it had caused fear and disruption during one of the busiest travel periods of the year.
The flight was delayed, with Alaska Airlines saying many passengers were transferred to other flights. The original service eventually departed at 11 a.m. local time.

articles.title: Nartatez vows impartiality after VP Sara slams PNP
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Sunday assured impartiality among its personnel after Vice President Sara Duterte earlier claimed that the organization has become "the enforcement arm of…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 3:26pm

The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Sunday assured impartiality among its personnel after Vice President Sara Duterte earlier claimed that the organization has become "the enforcement arm of politicians."

“As an institution, we remain guided by the Constitution, the rule of law, and our commitment to serve all Filipinos fairly and impartially, with every action grounded in facts, evidence, and due process,” said PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. in a statement.

“Impartiality is a principle that we strive to uphold in every police operation and public service. Our commitment is to treat everyone with fairness, respect, and compassion, while providing equal protection under the law regardless of one's position or political affiliation,” he added.

The PNP responded to Duterte after the latter told Nartatez "to refrain from paying lip service to the claim that the organization is apolitical—a claim that virtually every Filipino knows to be untrue."
The police earlier said there was "no rescue or release" of a former household staff member of the Vice President and four other individuals.
The PNP pointed out that the concerned former staff members of Duterte were not being held captive when police accompanied their lawyers to a hotel in Taguig City on November 17.
In its latest statement, the PNP said that two legal counsels sought assistance from Fort Bonifacio Police Sub-Station 1 and requested police personnel to accompany them to the hotel.

It added that the five persons voluntarily went with police personnel to the police station. But they declined to execute affidavits regarding their alleged captivity and did not identify any person responsible for the supposed threats or coercion.

“The PNP remains ready to listen, receive complaints, and provide appropriate police assistance to anyone who feels threatened or unsafe. We will act on every report in accordance with established procedures," said Nartatez. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: India: Nepal PM Balendra Shah heads to Delhi for first bilateral visit
articles.summary: Nepal's rapper-turned-prime minister Balendra Shah is in New Delhi for his first foreign bilateral trip since taking office. He is expected to discuss flood recovery, trade and energy in his talks…

image.caption: Former rappy Shah is Nepal's youngest ever prime minister Image: Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: November 22, 2026
Nepal PM Balendra Shah set to arrive in Delhi
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is set to arrive in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day visit, his first bilateral trip since taking office in March.
The 36-year-old former rapper will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. He will also meet Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and briefly visit President Droupadi Murmu.

Reconstruction after August's devastating floods is expected to dominate the talks. The disaster left some 1,500 dead and more than 5,200 missing, with roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes destroyed.
Nepal estimates rebuilding will cost $4.78 billion.
Nepal flood victims come to terms with massive loss
Nepal is also pressing for an extra route for commercial flights to Bhairahawa and Pokhara.

"India is a major and important partner for Nepal," Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters, saying the leaders would discuss trade, transit, investment, energy, connectivity and infrastructure.
New Delhi said the visit "reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal," AFP reported. Local media reported that talks may also touch upon unresolved border disputes.

India is Nepal's largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60% of its imports, worth $8.6 billion, versus China's 13%, according to World Bank figures. India and China regularly compete for influence in Nepal.
Shah will be accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal.

articles.title: Lacson flags P241B in 'fragmented ayuda' in 2027 budget
articles.summary: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Sunday criticized P241 billion worth of fragmented assistance programs in the Senate version of the proposed 2027 national budget, saying these would not generate the…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 3:12pm

Senator Panfilo Lacson on Sunday criticized P241 billion worth of fragmented assistance programs in the Senate version of the proposed 2027 national budget, saying these would not generate the productive investments needed to revive the economy.
In a social media post, Lacson said the amount was already lower than the P263 billion allocated for similar items in the House version of the General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

"True. Government construction plunged by -29% as shown by the January-September 2026 national accounts. Agriculture, forestry and fishing: -4.8%; industry: flat; investment: public construction down 15.1% as you mentioned," the senator said.

Lacson said the Senate should reconsider the allocations, arguing that the P241 billion in "fragmented" aid programs and funding for thousands of multipurpose buildings would not address the country's economic concerns.

"In relation to the 2027 budget measure which the Senate will tackle next week, I will insist that these concerns cannot be addressed by the P241B in fragmented ‘ayudas’ in the Senate version - already reduced from the House GAB’s P263B; and 3,950 multi-purpose buildings, on top of another 1,584 MPB’s under the LGSF-Financial Assistance to LGU sub program," he said.
These are not expenditure investments, but patronage aka ‘papogi’ spending," Lacson added.
He also questioned funding for 3,950 multipurpose buildings (MPBs), on top of 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) from 2022 to 2026.
Lacson said these allocations were examples of patronage-driven spending rather than productive investments, which the government should prioritize amid slowing economic growth and rising inflation.
He cited the 2.1% gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the third quarter of 2026, down from 2.4% in the second quarter, as well as inflation rising to 7.8% in October from 7.2% in September.

The senator also questioned allocations for the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP), Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) and Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS).
He said funding for MAIFIP should instead be coursed through the Universal Health Care program, which is already mandated by law.
Lacson argued that these assistance programs were not needs-based, claiming that beneficiaries were often determined by their connections to political sponsors rather than their eligibility.

“Again, this is patronage-driven. Those who benefit are the ones with connections. It is not needs-based. It is like having a sponsor or a political backer who gets you assistance, even if you are not qualified or deserving,” he said.

Initial findings on the proposed 2027 budget also showed that several multipurpose buildings had received appropriations in 2024, 2025 and 2026, but no structures had been built at their designated sites as of 2026.
Lacson said the Senate should prioritize spending that would stimulate economic activity when it takes up the 2027 budget measure next week.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Fire at confectionary factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
articles.summary:
Relatives of the missing victims flocked to the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones

A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36…

blocks.text: A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.

Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex. Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.
Relatives of the missing victims flocked near the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones, footage aired by local broadcasters showed.

blocks.caption: A drone view of emergency crews gathered outside the factory in Indonesia’s Banten province. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in Cikande in Indonesia’s Banten province about 50km from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, search and rescue official Rizky Dwianto said on Sunday.
“All elements of the joint SAR [search-and-rescue] team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritising the safety of personnel in the field,” he added.
Rizky said four people were injured and taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic.
Firefighters were alerted about 4.30pm on Saturday and found the building already engulfed in flames when they arrived, fire official Tubagus Machfudz told local broadcaster Kompas TV.

blocks.caption: Smoke rises from the factory on Sunday. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: “When we arrived … a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company’s protection system was functioning properly or not,” he said.
The Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters overnight that an estimated 60 people were inside the factory when it caught fire.
The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said in an Instagram post on Sunday.

blocks.caption: Crews from Indonesia’s Basarnas search and rescue agency inspect the site. Photograph: BASARNAS/AP

blocks.text: Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.
In December last year, a blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building in Jakarta and killed at least 22 people, police said.
In 2023, at least 13 people were killed in the country’s east after an explosion at a nickel-processing plant.

articles.title: Sara Duterte spox given until Nov. 23 to respond to Senate show-cause order
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte"s spokesperson Paolo Panelo has until Monday, November 23, to respond to the show-cause order issued against him by the Senate impeachment court over his remarks…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 3:09pm

Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo has until Monday, November 23, to respond to the show-cause order issued against him by the Senate impeachment court over his remarks questioning the impartiality of several senator-judges.
Senate impeachment court clerk Renato Bantug said the order was sent to Panelo via email on Friday, November 20.
“By email sent last [Friday] ang show cause order vs Paolo Panelo, given until tomorrow to respond,” Bantug said.
The show-cause order stemmed from Panelo’s remarks alleging that some senator-judges were acting as prosecutors in Duterte’s impeachment trial.
Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo raised the matter on Day 45 of the proceedings, asking Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero if the court could take action on Panelo’s statements.
Panelo, however, maintained that his remarks were protected by his constitutional right to free speech.

“I welcome the opportunity to demonstrate that my comments were fair, made in good faith, and did not impede, obstruct, or degrade the administration of justice, and are thus constitutionally protected,” he said in an earlier statement.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Gilas Hiraya out to chase Philippine women’s basketball dreams
articles.summary: Armed with a new name and fresh off an Asian Games silver-medal breakthrough, Gilas Hiraya sets its sights on historic women’s basketball milestones in 2027

blocks.text: STALWARTS. Gilas Hiraya stars Amyah Español (left) and Kacey dela Rosa hope to carve out a new era for Philippine women’s basketball.
UAAP
Armed with a new name and fresh off an Asian Games silver-medal breakthrough, Gilas Hiraya sets its sights on historic women’s basketball milestones in 2027

items: The Philippine women's basketball team has been rebranded as Gilas Hiraya to establish its own identity and aspirations ahead of significant competitions, including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The name 'Hiraya,' meaning dreams, hopes, and aspirations in Tagalog, was chosen to reflect the team's unique identity and to inspire women in the Philippines beyond basketball.

The team has seen recent success, including a silver medal at the Asian Games, and players express gratitude for the support and recognition of their hard work and dedication to growing women's basketball in the country.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Shifting to a refreshed identity, the newly christened Gilas Hiraya looks to bear the fruit of the hoop-crazy nation’s hopes, dreams, and aspirations in a huge 2027.
Gilas Hiraya, the new name of the Philippine women’s basketball team, was unveiled this month to establish its own identity as an emerging force in Asian hoops.

The rebrand comes ahead of a pivotal year in which both the 3×3 and 5-on-5 squads will chase a spot in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, alongside the country’s hosting of the FIBA Women’s Asia Cup at the SM Seaside Arena in Cebu next year.
“It’s really a deliberate decision to give them an identity of their own in order to shape a pathway that is unique for them,” Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas (SBP) executive director Erika Dy said.
“We don’t want them to just follow the footsteps of the men’s team or the men’s program,” she added. “We want them to be able to create their own dreams and aspirations for Philippine basketball.”
According to Dy, the idea of giving the women’s team its own name was suggested by FIBA secretary general Andreas Zagklis during a meeting in Shenzhen, China, in July 2025.
Zagklis pushed for the rebrand upon learning that the women’s team used to be known as “Perlas Pilipinas” before aligning its identity with the broader Gilas Pilipinas program in 2019.

Following lengthy discussions with numerous stakeholders, including the UAAP and the players themselves, Hiraya stood out among the other shortlisted names and was officially picked by the SBP on October 27.
“Part of why we chose the word Hiraya, which represents dreams, hopes, and aspirations — it’s a deep Tagalog word,” explained Dy, herself a former basketball player and coach for Ateneo.
“It’s because we really believe that our women’s program can represent that for all the women in the Philippines. It actually goes beyond basketball.”
With a fresh identity, Gilas Hiraya is riding a wave of sustained success, buoyed by a 3×3 silver-medal finish at the Asian Games and a deep tournament run by the 5-on-5 squad in the same meet.
Helping lead the way are Asiad silver medalists Kacey dela Rosa of Ateneo and Amyah Español of Far Eastern University.

“I’m just grateful that we have our own identity now as a women’s basketball team. And I just think every player on the women’s team is very dedicated to growing the sport of women’s basketball in the Philippines,” said Español.
“I’m just thankful that we have such a great support system who believes in us to have our own identity as the women’s team.”
For Dela Rosa, a two-time UAAP MVP, the identity shift reflects the program’s continued development under program director Bacon Austria and head coach BT Toews.

“As Filipinos, we put in a lot of work, like hard work, and we want them to know how much hard work we put in and sacrifices outside the court,” Dela Rosa said. “We also want them to recognize us — we are a team that dreams big.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: COP31 climate talks close to final deal, says summit president
articles.summary: The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks

blocks.text: JUSTICE. A member of Fridays for Future holds a placard at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 16, 2026.
Umit Bektas/Reuters
The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks

ANTALYA, Turkey – UN climate talks in Turkey approached a final deal on Sunday, November 22, with the announcement of a new package that COP31 presidents Australia and Turkey hope will achieve consensus on how to advance the fight against global warming.
The new draft deal was released two days after the conference in Antalya was scheduled to end.

If approved, it would acknowledge for the first time that global warming is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius (2.7-degree Fahrenheit) threshold that countries had sought to preserve, while calling for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse the overshoot.

The draft omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the center of the fractious talks. Instead, it includes language referring to a previous COP at which governments had agreed to transition away from oil, gas, and coal.
“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a plenary session early on Sunday.
He said the conference would reconvene in the morning to approve the deal.
Environmental group 350.org said it was disappointed by the draft’s failure to mention fossil fuels explicitly, as well as its encouragement of carbon-removal technologies.

“Carbon capture is one of the biggest scams of the overshoot era, and our leaders are on the verge of falling for it,” said Sara Shaw, the group’s campaigns and networks director, referring to the practice of trapping carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere.
Shaw said the draft deal opens the door to more fossil fuel development.
Observers to the closed-door talks said Saudi Arabia and other big oil-producer nations had pushed hard in negotiations for keeping fossil fuels out of the text, and carbon removal in.
A representative for the Saudi delegation declined to comment.

The new text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is leading the talks, Turkey, which is hosting the meeting, and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.
The presidency gave delegations several hours to raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 0700 GMT to begin approving it.

Australia’s task, supported by Turkey, has been to find a deal that balances the needs of nations most vulnerable to climate change with those whose economies depend on either the production or consumption of fossil fuels.

This year’s COP is the first since the UN’s environmental body confirmed that the rise in global temperature was set to blow past 1.5 degrees, a threshold all countries agreed over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Comelec dismisses 'no-el' in 2028 claims anew
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has once again dismissed resurfacing claims that there will be a “no-el” (no elections) scenario in 2028 as it emphasized that the poll…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has once again dismissed resurfacing claims that there will be a “no-el” (no elections) scenario in 2028 as it emphasized that the poll body is currently preparing for the much-anticipated elections.
In an interview with dzBB on Sunday, Comelec chair George Erwin Garcia was asked about recent claims that there will be no elections in 2028.

“Imposibleng mangyari. Ang Saligang Batas ang nagsasabing may eleksyon sa 2028. Walang kahit na anong batas ang pwedeng gawin ng kongreso, pirmahan ng pangulo ang makakapagbago sa Saligang Batas. Therefore, 100 percent naming ginagarantiya sa sambayanan na may halalan po tayo sa 2028.,” Garcia answered.

(That is impossible to happen. The 1987 Constitution says that there shall be elections in 2028. The Congress cannot make any law that will be signed by the president to change the Constitution. Therefore, we guarantee 100 percent that there will be elections in 2028.)

The Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution mandates that the president and vice president of the country must be elected for a term of six years, with their terms beginning at noon on the 30th day of June of the same election year.

This came after Atty. Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, said in an interview with Bilyonaryo News Channel that he had a conversation with Duterte where she said that she received information for a “no-el” plan in 2028.
Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez on Thursday debunked the claims that members of House of Representatives are forming plans to postpone the 2028 elections.
Garcia then said that the elections for the president and vice president cannot be likened to Barangay and Sangguniang Elections where they can be postponed or have their terms shortened or extended.
“Sa president and vice president, di pwedeng baguhin ang termino sapagkat wala tayong hold over capacity. Matatapos at matatapos ang kanilang termino, June 30 tanghali ng 2028,” he added.
(The terms of the president and vice president cannot be changed because we don’t have a hold over capacity. Their terms will end at noon of June 30, 2028.)
Election preparations
Garcia also shared updates on Comelec’s preparations for the 2028 elections, noting that the filing of certificates of candidacy (COC) will be scheduled on September 20-26, 2027.

Garcia earlier said that the poll body will open the period filing of COCs earlier than the usual timeline of the first week of October so they can resolve disputes on candidacies and can immediately start printing of official ballots.

Aside from this, he said that the poll body began the bidding process for the internet voting system and transmission services. He added that the procurement process for the automated counting machines (ACMs) will start by December this year.

Garcia also said that the poll body will allocate P22 billion for the leasing of the ACMs, which is the same mechanism it used for the 2025 midterm elections. However, he clarified that the ACMs used in the previous elections will not be used in the 2028 elections as the machines have to be brand new. /ms

articles.title: DENR encourages cycling for cleaner air
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources on Sunday encouraged the public to consider using a bicycle as an alternative mode of transportation to address air pollution in the country.

blocks.text: NATIONAL BICYCLE DAY
Published November 22, 2026 2:28pm

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) on Sunday encouraged the public to consider using a bicycle as an alternative mode of transportation to address air pollution in the country.
The department also highly suggested to the public to consider walking or riding a bicycle for short trips.

“As I have always said, everyone can help fight climate change. When we rethink our ways of travelling, when we walk or ride a bike instead of driving, we become part of the solution to the climate crisis,” said DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna in a statement.
The National Bicycle Day, which is observed every fourth Sunday of November under Proclamation No. 1052, falls on November 22 this year.
The DENR also launched the Bike-to-Work Campaign for its personnel, which encourages department employees to get into cycling.

"The Department's campaign seeks to encourage sustained cycling among its workforce beyond the annual celebration. The initiative, undertaken in partnership with the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) and the DoTr Active Transport Project Office (ATPO), aims to promote active mobility, reduce dependence on motorized transportation, and contribute to cleaner air and lower greenhouse gas emissions," the DENR said.
"It will also feature a GHG (Greenhouse Gases) Calculator that will help employees estimate benefits of their work-related bicycle commutes," it added.
There are concentrations of particulate matter (PM) 2.5 in the air, according to the Manila Observatory.

The common sources of PM 2.5 pollution in Metro Manila are motor vehicle exhaust, construction site dust, road dust, practices related to waste management, and the burning of organic matter, known as biomass burning. Contributions also come from natural sources, such as sea salt. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/KG, GMA News

articles.title: No bias among senator-judges, part of our job is to test credibility of witnesses-- Win Gatchalian
articles.summary: Senator Sherwin Gatchalian on Sunday dismissed claims that some senator-judges were biased in the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, saying their role is to assess the…

blocks.text: Published November 22, 2026 2:18pm

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian on Sunday dismissed claims that some senator-judges were biased in the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, saying their role is to assess the credibility of witnesses.

“Kasama 'yan sa trabaho ng senator-judges to test the credibility nung testigo, lalo na may mga testigo na nakakalimot, hindi alam. Wala kang choice to test the credibility at to test kung sino itong taong ito. Ginagawa rin naman 'yun ng Prosekusyon, ginagawa rin naman ng Defense 'yun– pwede ring gawin ng senator-judges 'yun,” Gatchalian told Super Radyo dzBB.

(Part of the senator-judges' job is to test the credibility of witnesses, especially if some forget things or don't know the answers. They have no choice but to test the credibility of the witness and determine who this person is. The Prosecution does it, the Defense does it, and the senator-judges can also do it.)

“Pagdating sa bias, dalawang panig 'yan: pwede kang maging bias for the respondent or against the respondent. Pero nakikita naman natin na as much as possible, 'yung mga senato-judge natin ay objective ang pagtatanong natin,” he added.
(When it comes to bias, you can be biased for or against the respondent. But we can see that, as much as possible, our senator-judges are asking questions objectively.)

Gatchalian made the statement after the Senate impeachment court issued a show-cause order against Duterte’s spokesperson, lawyer Paolo Panelo, over his comments regarding the alleged partiality of several senator-judges.
Panelo had asserted that some senator-judges were acting as prosecutors.
Following the issuance of a show-cause order, Panelo invoked his right to free speech in making critical statements about senator-judges.

"I welcome the opportunity to demonstrate that my comments were fair, made in good faith, and did not impede, obstruct, or degrade the administration of justice, and are thus constitutionally protected," hee said.
Panelo assured that he would formally respond to the show cause order within the prescribed period upon receiving it. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Dozens missing as deadly fire hits Indonesian candy factory
articles.summary: A fire at a confectionery factory in Indonesia's Banten province has killled at least three people. Dozens are also unaccounted for after the blaze, which destroyed large parts of the facility.

image.caption: The fire broke out on Saturday afternoonImage: Mohammad Hashemi Rafsanjani/AFP

blocks.text: Indonesian rescue teams are searching for 36 workers who remained unaccounted for after a fire at a candy-making factory killed at least three people, officials said on Sunday.
The fire occurred at the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, around 50 kilometers (31 miles) west of the capital, Jakarta, in the Serang district of Banten province.
What do we know about the Indonesian confectionery factory fire?
The factory caught fire on Saturday afternoon, local search and rescue agency official Rizky Dwianto said.
"All elements of the joint SAR (search-and-rescue) team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritizing the safety of personnel in the field," he added.
Rizky said four people injured in the blaze had been taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic. Eleven more were said to have been rescued alive.

blocks.caption: Rescue teams have been scouring the factory for survivorsImage: BASARNAS/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The governor of Banten province, Andra Soni, told reporters overnight that 60 people were believed to have been inside the factory when the fire broke out.
Drone footage shows the fire destroyed large sections of the three-story building, bringing down the roof in some places.
Survivors said the fire started in a cooling unit on the third floor.
The factory produces Milkita, an Indonesian brand of milk-based candies and snack products.
Deadly industrial fires in Indonesia
Indonesia has seen a series of deadly industrial fires in recent years, raising questions about the country's workplace safety standards into question.
Among other disasters, at least 22 people were killed in a fire last December that broke out in a seven-story building in Jakarta after a suspected drone battery explosion, police said.
An explosion in a nickel-processing plant in the east of the country killed at least 13 people in 2023.

articles.title: Dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
articles.summary: At least three people were killed and four injured in a fire at a confectionary factory over the weekend.

blocks.text: At least three people have been killed and 36 were still missing after a fire at a confectionary factory in western Java on Saturday.
Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for the missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.
Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.
The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.
Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire.

Photos and footage of the scene showed the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.
"All members of the joint SAR team are making every effort to locate the missing victims while prioritising the safety of personnel on the ground," the rescue agency said.
Relatives of the missing workers had gathered outside the factory waiting for updates, according to local broadcasts cited by AFP.
Firefighters had been called to the building at 1630 local time (0930 GMT) but it was already engulfed in flames, broadcaster Kompas TV reported, citing fire official Tubugas Machfudz.
"When we arrived (on location)... a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company's protection system was functioning properly or not," he said.
The factory is owned by PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, according to search and rescue authorities.
On LinkedIn the company describes itself as a subsidiary of UNIFAM, one of Indonesia's largest food and beverage companies.
